newsitem.title: INDIA: India to launch 14-day intermediate treasury bills.
newsitem.headline: India to launch 14-day intermediate treasury bills.

text.p: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) said on Monday it had introduced with immediate effect a 14-day intermediate treasury bill programme to replace the 91-day tap treasury bills which will be discontinued from April 1, 1997.

"Following the finance minister's announcement in the budget for 1997/98 and the agreement signed between the Reserve Bank of India and the government of India on March 26, 1997, the 91-day tap treasury bills will be discontinued with effect from April 1, 1997," RBI said in a statement.

"In order to provide them with an alternative arrangement in place of the 91-day tap treasury bills for investment of their temporary cash surpluses effective April 1, 1997, the government has introduced the scheme of 14-day intermediate treasury bills," the RBI said.
The following are the salient features of the new instrument.
+ Eligibility: The bills will be sold only to state governments, foreign central banks and other specified bodies with whom the RBI has an arrangment.
+ Minimum investment: the 14-day intermediate treasury bills would be sold for a minimum amount of 100,000 rupees and in multiples of 100,000 rupees.
+ Form: They will be issued only in book-entry form, that is by credit to subsidiary general ledger account.
+ Transferability: these bills are not transferable.
+ Repayment: These bills will be repaid/renewed at par on the expiration of 14 days from the date of issue.

+ Discount rate: The discount rate on these bills will be set at quarterly intervels so that effective yield of this instrument will be equivalent to the interest rate on ways and means advances chargeable to the federal government.
+ Rediscounting: The bills will be rediscounted at 50 basis points higher than the discount rate. On rediscounting, they will be extinguished.
The state governments will continue to participate as 'non-competitive' bidders in 91-day treasury bill auctions.
